question_title: Will a Senate cloture motion related to the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) be filed before August 8, 2026?
summary: The question asks only whether a cloture motion is FILED (not passed) on H.R. 3633 between July 25 and August 7, 2026 — a lower bar than passage. As of July 24, no cloture motion had been filed and no floor vote scheduled. The strongest YES driver is Thune's July 23 statement that he hopes to "get Clarity started" in its Senate floor process; because the bill is contested, lacks 60 votes, and Democrats won't grant unanimous consent while still negotiating, a genuine "start" would mechanically require filing cloture on a motion to proceed. Against this: Thune's overall framing is pessimistic ("won't pass"), the immediate priority next week is a Russia sanctions bill, the final pre-recess week is crowded with appropriations/NDAA, the deal is unfinished (~2 of 5-7 Democratic votes), and leaders often avoid filing doomed cloture votes. Factor-implied probability sits ~41%, but I discount toward the status-quo anchor given the hedged, pessimistic leadership signal and crowded calendar. Landing at ~31%.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, between July 25, 2026 and 11:59 p.m. ET on August 7, 2026 (inclusive), a cloture motion is filed in the U.S. Senate on H.R. 3633 (the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, "CLARITY Act") — whether a cloture motion on a motion to proceed to the bill, on the bill itself, on a substitute amendment to it, or on any related measure whose text is the CLARITY Act. Filing is the presentation of the cloture motion on the Senate floor under Senate Rule XXII; an actual cloture vote is NOT required. Resolution is based on the "All Actions" record for H.R. 3633 on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633/all-actions) and/or the official U.S. Senate cloture motions list (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/cloture/), or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) if those are unavailable. A value of one or more qualifying cloture motions filed in the window resolves YES; zero resolves NO.
fine_print: If the CLARITY Act's text is taken up on the Senate floor under a different bill or measure number (e.g., a Senate companion or a vehicle carrying the same market-structure language) and a cloture motion is filed on that measure in the window, that counts as a qualifying filing. A unanimous-consent agreement to proceed without any cloture motion being filed does not count. Cloture motions filed before July 25, 2026 do not count.
